hypotheses.reasoning: search-api heap climbs steadily from ~37% at 02:56 to 78% after full GC at 03:02 (#474) with old gen not reclaimed and GC overhead rising; 87% and 35% GC overhead at 03:05 (#708). The in-process productCache is never reclaimed, leading to java.lang.OutOfMemoryError at productCache.put (#912), then the container is OOMKilled against its 2Gi limit (#914), and another worker pod dies with OOM (#1050, #1051). Each restart re-warms the cache (#931, #1077), so the memory pressure recurs in bursts. Web-bff 502s on GET /search (#994, #1138, #1327, #1381) are 'upstream search-api connection reset (no healthy upstream)' during pods being down, i.e. downstream symptoms. Redis shows evicted=0 throughout, so the leak is in the search-api process, not the shared cache. Analytics-forwarder 429s (#481 onward) are a separate noisy side issue that doesn't touch the search path.
Analytics-ingest 429 retry storms are a plausible noise source but they only affect analytics-forwarder, not search-api memory or the GET /search path; no evidence they drove search-api heap growth.

verdict.recommendedAction: Treat as a search-api memory leak in productCache (no bounded eviction). Immediately: roll search-api pods/raise memory headroom to stop the restart loop, and drain/bound productCache (size cap/TTL). Verify heap after restart stays flat. Follow up with a fix to the cache eviction in search-api v1.8.8 and a heap-growth alert at ~70%. Separately, look at analytics-forwarder's 429 retry/drop behavior, which is unrelated to this 502 burst.
